To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
limited gastrectomy for early gastric cancer with negative sentinel node biopsy is feasible and safe.
SN-navigated gastrectomy with limited resection of the stomach and lymph nodes is feasible and safe for patients with early gastric cancer.
limited gastrectomy is feasible and safe when combined with SN navigation and dissection of SN station in early gastric cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the early results of SN-navigated gastrectomy in the treatment of patients with gastric cancer.
the use of the sentinel lymph node (SLN) concept for gastric cancer surgery.
the development and validation of an integrated system for the detection and characterization of early-stage cancerous lesions in the gastrointestinal tract.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SN-navigated gastrectomy with limited dissection of SN station is a safe and acceptable option for patients with early gastric cancer.
limited gastrectomy for early gastric cancer is safe and acceptable if SNs are negative and SN stations are limited to either the greater or lesser curvature.
SN biopsy and dissection of SN station is a safe and effective method for the surgical management of T1N0 gastric cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SN biopsy should be mandatory for all patients with T1N gastric cancer and limited gastrectomy should be performed for patients with negative SN biopsy.
the SN-naviged limited surgery is a safe alternative to a standard procedure for T1N1M0 gastric cancer.
limited gastrectomy is safe for patients with early gastric cancer if SN stations are dissected.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SN biopsy alone is not enough, and dissection of SN station(s) is mandatory to avoid leaving metastasis behind.
the limited gastrectomy is feasible in the early stage of gastric cancer.
SN-navigated gastrectomy with limited resection is feasible and can reduce the extent of gastrectomy for patients with early gastric cancer.
